findings.issue_text: [BUG] This hunk rewrites the light-theme value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), producing a 70/30 pair that is the inverse of the intended pairing (every other hunk in this PR preserves the light value and adds 100-X for dark). In light themes the bold link that previously rendered dark (primary+30%) now renders as washed-out light gray (primary+70%) on a white background — a visible readability regression the PR title explicitly scopes out — and in dark themes it gets secondary+30% (very dim for a bold link) instead of the intended secondary+70%.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length pair is swapped: light theme now gets scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and dark theme scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%), the exact inverse of the identical selector in desktop/modal.scss (changed to 70/30 in this same PR) and of the pre-existing light value of 70%. Mobile light-theme modal hint text flips from light gray to dark and no longer matches desktop rendering of the same modal, while mobile dark-theme hint text becomes much lighter than desktop's; the pair should be 70/30.

[BUG] The .name light-theme value changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, diverging from common/base/user.scss which styles the same .name element at 30/70 in this same PR. Light-theme user profile name renders mid-gray instead of the previous darker gray, and desktop/mobile now disagree with the base stylesheet for the same element — evidence the 50% was a copy-paste default rather than the intended 30/70 pairing.

[BUG] The .name light-theme value changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, diverging from common/base/user.scss which keeps .name at 30/70 in this same PR. Mobile light-theme user profile name renders mid-gray instead of the previous darker gray and disagrees with both desktop and the base stylesheet for the same element.

[BUG] The h3 light-theme value changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50%, while the identical h3 in desktop/topic-post.scss is correctly changed to 20/80 in this same PR. Mobile light-theme small-action heading renders mid-gray instead of near-primary dark, so the same component renders differently on desktop and mobile in light themes.

[ADVISORY] The light/dark percentage pair X%/(100-X)% is hand-written at roughly 115 call sites across this diff with no shared helper, and five sites in this very diff already drifted (30→70, 70→30, and three normalized to 50/50), demonstrating the failure mode of this hand-maintained enumeration. Every future dark-theme pass must hand-verify two percentages per site and reviewers must mentally check sums; a single SCSS function wrapping dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $x), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $x)) would make the mismatched pairs in this diff unrepresentable and shrink each call site to one argument.

[BUG] The light-theme operand was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) — the mirror was applied to the wrong side — so this bold link renders at 70% lightness in light themes instead of the previous 30%. Every light-theme user sees this bold link fade from dark gray to a washed-out light gray; the dark operand (secondary 30%) proves the intended light value was 30%, i.e. an unintended light-mode regression in a PR scoped to dark themes.

[BUG] The .name light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, diverging from the parallel common/base/user.scss .name rule converted in this same diff which correctly keeps 30% in light mode. Light-theme users see the profile .name text lightened from 30% to 50% lightness while the same name renders at 30% on the common/user page — an inconsistent, unintended light-mode color change.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to 30%, contradicting the identical desktop/modal.scss .custom-message-length rule converted in this same diff which keeps 70% in light mode. Mobile light-theme users see the custom-message length hint jump from light gray to dark gray, rendering differently from the same hint on desktop — a transposition error (mirror applied to the wrong operand).

[BUG] The h3 light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50%, contradicting the identical desktop/topic-post.scss h3 rule converted in this same diff which keeps 20% in light mode. Mobile light-theme users see this heading drop from near-black to mid-gray while desktop keeps it near-black — an unintended light-mode regression, apparently copied from the adjacent h4's 50/50 pair.

[BUG] The .name light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, diverging from the parallel common/base/user.scss .name rule converted in this same diff which keeps 30% in light mode. Mobile light-theme users see the profile .name text lightened from 30% to 50% lightness, inconsistent with the same name on the common user page — an unintended light-mode change mirroring the identical desktop/user.scss error.

[ADVISORY] The sibling declaration color: darken($primary, 40%) in the .wmd-input rule is left unconverted while the adjacent .wmd-input:disabled background in the same hunk was migrated to dark-light-choose, so composer body text still derives from $primary alone with no $secondary fallback. Dark-theme users composing a reply get body text at a fixed darkened primary (~mid-gray on a near-black background) instead of a theme-adaptive value; the next dark-theme pass must revisit this exact selector the PR already touched.

[ADVISORY] The hardcoded background-color: white in .invalid .hex input survives inside the same rule block whose sibling .description line this diff converts for dark themes, leaving a non-theme-aware surface in the migrated path. Admins on dark schemes hit the invalid-hex error state and get a stark white input box inside an otherwise theme-adaptive screen, defeating the dark-theme correctness this PR claims for this file.

[ADVISORY] This ~60-declaration rewrite across 30+ stylesheets ships with no test, lint, or visual-regression check anywhere in the diff, and the rewrite has already introduced five silent light-theme value changes (30→70, 70→30, 20→50, 30→50 twice). Light-theme users absorb unreviewed color changes; a one-line mechanical invariant (light operand must equal the replaced scale-color value) would have caught all five regressions before merge.

[BUG] The light-theme branch was rewritten from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), so this hunk changes light-theme rendering instead of only adding a $secondary branch for dark themes. In light themes the bold link that previously rendered near 37% lightness now renders near 73% — dramatically fainter; the committed (70%, 30%) pair is the pre-existing value's complement with arguments swapped, and this is the only pattern in the PR where the light value was not preserved, indicating a swap typo rather than scoped work.

[BUG] The light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50%, altering light-theme rendering; the desktop twin of this same h3 rule (desktop/topic-post.scss:320) correctly keeps 20%. Mobile light-theme users get a much fainter section heading (≈28% → ≈55% lightness) and mobile no longer matches desktop for the same component — a light-theme change not traceable to the PR's stated dark-theme intent.

[BUG] The light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to 30%, reversing the pair relative to the identical .custom-message-length rule in desktop/modal.scss:94 which keeps 70%. Light-theme mobile modal hint text darkens from ≈73% to ≈37% lightness and renders differently from desktop for the same modal footer — unscoped light-theme drift, almost certainly the (70%, 30%) arguments entered in reverse.

[BUG] The .name light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50% while the adjacent .title in the same hunk keeps its original 50%, so this light-value drift is not traceable to the dark-theme requirement. Light-theme desktop profile names render fainter (≈37% → ≈55% lightness) than before the PR; if the intent was to normalize .name to .title's value, that is undocumented scope drift, and if not, it is a copy-paste of the ubiquitous 50/50 pair over a 30% site.

[BUG] The .name light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50% while the adjacent .title in the same hunk keeps its original 50%, mirroring the same unscoped light-value drift as desktop/user.scss:522. Light-theme mobile profile names render fainter (≈37% → ≈55% lightness) than before the PR — work outside the stated 'use $secondary for dark themes' intent with no justification anywhere in the change.

[ADVISORY] The invariant this PR establishes — dark branch lightness must equal 100 minus the light branch lightness of scale-color($secondary) — is hand-maintained at ~45 call sites across ~25 files with no SCSS helper function or lint rule to enforce it, and this very diff ships five sites where the hand-maintained pair or base value was botched. Every future scale-color($primary, $lightness:) call silently regresses dark themes again, and every hand-edit of a percentage risks exactly the swapped/drifted pairs introduced here; a single helper (e.g. @function muted-color($pct) { @return dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $pct), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $pct)); }) collapses each two-argument call to one argument and makes this entire defect class unrepresentable.

[ADVISORY] The dark-theme sweep stops one rule short: .invalid .hex input keeps a hardcoded background-color: white two lines below the .description rule this PR converted in the same block. In dark color schemes the admin badge hex input renders with a white background while its text inherits the scheme's light $primary, producing light-text-on-white and a glaring white box in the exact admin badge form section this PR otherwise fixes for dark themes.

[BUG] The two lightness values are swapped: the light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) while the dark branch received 30%, inverting the dark-light-choose(light-theme-value, dark-theme-value) convention (light keeps the original X, dark gets 100−X) followed by every other hunk in this PR. In light themes this bold link renders at primary+70% (~#d4d4d4, ~1.5:1 on a white background) instead of the previous primary+30% (~#6f6f6f, ~5:1) — effectively unreadable; in dark themes it renders at secondary+30% (~2.9:1 against the dark background) instead of the intended secondary+70%, so the element regresses in both modes. The correct form is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

[BUG] Same argument swap: the light branch changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to 30% and the dark branch got 70%, contradicting both this PR's own convention and the identical .custom-message-length rule in desktop/modal.scss, which correctly keeps 70%/30%. On mobile light themes the composer's character-count hint jumps from primary+70% (subtle, ~#d4d4d4) to primary+30% (~#6f6f6f), becoming far more prominent than designed, and in dark themes mobile now renders secondary+70% where desktop renders secondary+30% for the same class — the two platforms visibly disagree.

[BUG] The h3 replacement line duplicates the adjacent h4 replacement (50%/50%) instead of preserving the original light-theme 20%, so mobile diverges from desktop/topic-post.scss's matching h3, which keeps 20% (dark 80%). In mobile light themes this heading renders at primary+50% (~#a1a1a1, ~2.5:1 on white) instead of the previous primary+20% (~#5a5a5a, ~7:1) — washed-out heading text and a new desktop/mobile inconsistency produced by a copy-paste slip.

[BUG] The .name replacement reuses the adjacent .title values (50%/50%), silently changing the light-theme color from the original scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) in a PR whose stated scope is dark themes only. Light-theme users see this name render at primary+50% (~#a1a1a1) instead of primary+30% (~#6f6f6f), losing the emphasis the 30% value gave it; the change also diverges from common/base/user.scss, which in this same PR keeps .name at 30%/70%.

[BUG] Same copy-paste slip as desktop/user.scss: the .name replacement reuses the adjacent .title values (50%/50%), silently changing the light-theme color from the original scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). Mobile light-theme users see this name render at primary+50% (~#a1a1a1) instead of primary+30% (~#6f6f6f), losing emphasis and diverging from common/base/user.scss's .name, which this same PR keeps at 30%/70%.

[ADVISORY] In dark themes this rule now sets a background derived from $secondary (scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) while the adjacent &[href] branch pins the text color to $secondary itself — text and background derive from the same variable only 30 lightness points apart (~2.8:1), whereas the old dark-theme background clamped to near-white (~19:1 against $secondary text). Any linked .badge-notification count rendered by this rule in a dark theme drops from high contrast to borderline readability; the light-theme branch has the same structural weakness (primary+70% background under $secondary text, ~1.5:1), indicating the background/text pairing was never contrast-checked at either branch.

[ADVISORY] The PR hand-writes the invariant 'dark-branch lightness = 100 − light-branch lightness' at ~80 separate call sites instead of factoring it into a one-argument helper (e.g. @function dimmed($l) { @return dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $l), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $l)); }). The invariant is maintained only by copy-paste discipline, and this diff itself proves the drift is real: five sites already violate it (desktop/topic-post.scss ~291 and mobile/modal.scss ~102 swap the branches; mobile/topic-post.scss ~182, desktop/user.scss ~522 and mobile/user.scss ~497 copy the wrong source values). With the helper each site becomes a one-liner, the complementarity cannot drift, and the next muted-color addition carries no arithmetic risk.

[BUG] The light and dark values are transposed: the removed rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` but the replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, inverting the light-N%/dark-(100−N)% complement used at every other site in this PR. Light themes render this bold link ~40 lightness points lighter than the approved design (near-background contrast on white), and dark themes get scale-color($secondary, 30%) — a color barely lighter than the dark $secondary background, making the link nearly invisible; both themes diverge from the PR's stated scope of changing only dark-theme rendering.

[BUG] The light and dark values are transposed: the removed rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` but the replacement uses 30% for light themes and 70% for dark themes, the inverse of the complement pattern and of the identical `.custom-message-length` rule in desktop/modal.scss which correctly uses 70%/30%. Light-theme users see the modal footer hint text jump from light gray to a much darker gray — an unapproved visual change on mobile only — and mobile now renders this hint differently from desktop for the same modal, so the two surfaces silently diverge.

[BUG] The `.name` color's light-theme lightness was silently changed from 30% to 50% (dark branch 50% instead of the complement 70%), matching a copy of the adjacent `.title` line and diverging from both the removed rule and the parallel `.name` rule in common/base/user.scss which uses 30%/70%. Light-theme users see the user-header name rendered noticeably lighter with no accepted design change, and dark themes lose the intended name/title emphasis distinction (name now identical to .title at 50% instead of the brighter 70% complement used by the common stylesheet).

[BUG] The `.name` color's light-theme lightness was silently changed from 30% to 50% (dark branch 50% instead of the complement 70%), identical to the neighboring `.title` line and diverging from the removed 30% rule and from common/base/user.scss's 30%/70% `.name` rule. Light-theme mobile user header renders the name lighter than the approved design, and dark themes dim the name below the intended complement value; the pattern of the error (matching the adjacent .title line) indicates copy-paste drift, not an accepted objective change.

[BUG] The suggested-topic `h3` color's light-theme lightness was silently changed from 20% to 50% (dark branch 50% instead of the complement 80%), diverging from the removed rule and from the same h3 in desktop/topic-post.scss which correctly uses 20%/80%. Light-theme mobile users see suggested-topic headings drop from near-primary emphasis to mid-gray, flattening the heading/subtitle hierarchy (h3 and h4 now render identically at 50%), an objective change to light-theme appearance nowhere stated or accepted in this PR.

[ADVISORY] The dark-theme complement (dark lightness = 100 − light lightness) is hand-computed inline at ~90 call sites across 25 stylesheets instead of being computed by a helper such as `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $l), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $l))`. Every future sweep of this pattern re-invites exactly the transposition/copy-paste errors this PR ships at five sites (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, mobile/user.scss:497); a single helper would make the complement mechanical, reduce each call site to one parameter, and make the five defects introduced here impossible to write.

[BUG] The light-theme value was transposed with the dark-theme value: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light branch renders a different color than before this PR. In light themes this bold `a` link jumps from 30% to 70% lightness — a ~40-point lightening that washes out its contrast on light backgrounds — while every other site in this ~100-site sweep preserves the light value and the PR title scopes the change to dark themes only.

[BUG] The `.name` rule's light-theme value changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` — the dark-light-choose pair was copy-pasted from the adjacent `.title` rule instead of preserving the original 30%. Light-theme users see the profile header name rendered noticeably lighter than before and now identical in color to `.title`, erasing the intended visual hierarchy between the two lines; the change is outside the PR's dark-theme-only scope.

[BUG] The `.name` rule's light-theme value changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, duplicating the same copy-paste-from-`.title` error made in desktop/user.scss:522. Light-theme mobile users see the profile header name noticeably lighter than before and identical to `.title`, with no desktop/mobile consistency justification since the pre-PR value (30%) differed from `.title` (50%) in both layouts.

[BUG] The `.custom-message-length` light-theme value was transposed: old `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` became light branch `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, while the identical desktop rule (desktop/modal.scss:94) correctly kept 70%/30%. In light themes the modal hint text renders ~40 points darker than before, appearing far more prominent than the intended muted hint, and mobile and desktop now render the same element with different light-theme colors.

[BUG] The `h3` light-theme value changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, while the same rule in desktop/topic-post.scss:321 correctly preserved 20% with an 80% dark complement. Light-theme mobile users see this heading rendered much lighter than intended and lighter than the same heading on desktop — a silent visual regression introduced by copy-pasting the 50/50 pair used elsewhere in the diff instead of the 20/80 pair.

[ADVISORY] The diff hand-maintains an implicit invariant at ~100 call sites — dark-branch `$secondary` lightness must equal 100 minus the light-branch `$primary` lightness — with no single source of truth, and this very diff violates it at 5 sites (desktop/topic-post.scss:291, desktop/user.scss:522, mobile/user.scss:497, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182). Every future value tweak or dark-theme sweep must hand-compute the complement at each site and will keep producing transpositions at this rate; a SCSS helper (e.g. `@function muted-color($p) { @return dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $p), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $p)); }`) reduces each site to one argument, deleting the second hand-written value and the entire transposition error class demonstrated above.

[BUG] The light-theme value was altered, not just the dark theme added: the bold link rule changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light branch no longer matches the original color. In light themes (dark $primary on white $secondary) the link renders at ~83% lightness instead of ~43% — near-white bold text on a white background, effectively unreadable; every other hunk in this PR preserves the light value and only adds the complementary $secondary branch, and the dark branch here even received the complementary 30%, confirming the light/dark pair was swapped by mistake.

[BUG] The light-theme value of `.custom-message-length` was inverted: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` became a dark-light-choose whose light branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, while the identical class in desktop/modal.scss (line 94) correctly keeps 70% light / 30% dark. In light themes the modal hint text jumps from subtle light gray (~83% lightness) to dark gray (~43%), becoming visually prominent and inconsistent with the same modal footer hint on desktop; the dark branch (70% on $secondary) shows the light/dark values were swapped.

[BUG] The light-theme value of the quoted/embedded-post `h3` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to 50%, whereas the identical h3 rule in desktop/topic-post.scss (line ~321) keeps 20% and only adds `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)` for dark themes. In light themes the embedded-post title drops from a dark, prominent heading (~33% lightness) to washed-out mid-gray (~63%), de-emphasizing it and diverging from how the same component renders on desktop.

[BUG] The light-theme value of `.names .name` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 50%, while the corresponding `.name` rule in common/base/user.scss (line ~124) keeps 30% and only adds `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for dark themes. In light themes the username renders noticeably lighter than before (~63% vs ~43% lightness) and inconsistently with the base stylesheet's `.name` rule for the same element; the PR's stated scope is dark-theme fixes only, so this light-mode change is out of scope and unflagged by the PR title.

[BUG] The light-theme value of `.names .name` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 50%, mirroring the same out-of-scope light-mode change made in desktop/user.scss line 522 while common/base/user.scss's `.name` keeps 30% light / 70% dark. In light themes the mobile username renders lighter than before and inconsistent with the base stylesheet's `.name` rule; if the 30%→50% shift was not intentional, both user.scss sites need the light branch restored to 30% with 70% on $secondary for the dark branch.

[BUG] The light-theme value of this bold link's color was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) — the dark/light pair was written swapped — so light themes now render the link at ~83% lightness instead of the original dark value. Light-theme users get a washed-out, near-invisible bold link on the light post background (with default colors ~#d4d4d4 on white, contrast ~1.4:1); a PR scoped to dark themes silently regresses light theme.

[BUG] The light-theme value of .custom-message-length was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to 30% — swapped relative to the identical .custom-message-length rule in desktop/modal.scss, which correctly keeps 70% for light — so the light-theme branch now carries the dark-theme-intended value. Light-theme mobile users see the custom-message-length hint as dark, prominent text instead of the intended light-gray hint, and mobile diverges from desktop for the same component.

[BUG] The h3 light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50%, while the mirrored h3 in desktop/topic-post.scss keeps 20% and adds secondary 80% for dark — the light-theme heading color regresses to mid-gray. Light-theme mobile users see this heading washed out from near-black to mid-gray, and mobile and desktop render the same component differently under the same light color scheme.

[BUG] The .name light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, making it identical to the adjacent .title rule, while common/base/user.scss in this same PR preserves 30% for .name — the light-theme value was altered instead of preserved. Light-theme users lose the darker full-name emphasis in the profile header (name and title render in the same mid-gray); the change contradicts the PR's dark-theme-only scope.

[BUG] The .name light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, making it identical to the adjacent .title rule, while common/base/user.scss in this same PR preserves 30% for .name — the light-theme value was altered instead of preserved. Light-theme mobile users lose the darker full-name emphasis in the profile header (name and title render in the same mid-gray); the change contradicts the PR's dark-theme-only scope.

[ADVISORY] This diff hand-writes over 110 dark-light-choose pairs whose two lightness arguments must sum to 100%, and five of them are already wrong (swapped or normalized), demonstrating that the hand-maintained pairing is the defect factory in this change. Every future edit to any of these declarations requires the maintainer to mentally compute the complement, so the next sweep keeps producing silent light-theme regressions like the five in this PR; a one-argument helper wrapping dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $l), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $l)) deletes the second hand-written value at every site and makes the swap impossible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR hand-writes the invariant 'dark-branch lightness = 100 − light-branch lightness' at ~80 separate call sites instead of factoring it into a one-argument helper (e.g. @function dimmed($l) { @return dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: $l), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100% - $l)); }). The invariant is maintained only by copy-paste discipline, and this diff itself proves the drift is real: five sites already violate it (desktop/topic-post.scss ~291 and mobile/modal.scss ~102 swap the branches; mobile/topic-post.scss ~182, desktop/user.scss ~522 and mobile/user.scss ~497 copy the wrong source values). With the helper each site becomes a one-liner, the complementarity cannot drift, and the next muted-color addition carries no arithmetic risk.

adjudication.rationale: While the diff clearly repeats the same `dark-light-choose(scale-color(...), scale-color(...))` pattern many times (so a helper could be a reasonable refactor), the finding’s central claim that the diff "proves drift is real" because "five sites already violate" the stated invariant `secondary_lightness = 100 - primary_lightness` is not supported. In the cited examples the pairs shown in the diff still satisfy complementarity (e.g., 70/30, 30/70, 50/50). What *is* visible is that a few locations changed the primary lightness value compared to before (e.g. desktop/topic-post.scss around the `a { color: ...70%/30% }` change), but that is not the same as violating the 100−L invariant, and intent can’t be proven from the diff alone.
